title: NIN Knowledge Commons Doctrine
creator: Robert Domondon
claims_supported: Knowledge Packs are authoritative while indexes are rebuildable derivatives.
Retrieved content does not confer clinical or institutional authority.
Authorization and lifecycle filtering precede retrieval.
limitations: Proposed Commons doctrine; not institutional policy or clinical authority.

title: NIN Knowledge Commons Operational Playbook
creator: Robert Domondon
claims_supported: Public Packs must remain no-PHI and rights-aware.
AI-generated material requires human verification.
Publication and retrieval require explicit lifecycle controls.
limitations: Proposed manual-first playbook; listed capabilities are not automatically operational.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
creator: National Institute of Standards and Technology
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
claims_supported: AI risk management should consider impacts to individuals, organizations, and society.
Trustworthiness considerations belong throughout AI design, use, and evaluation.
limitations: Voluntary general framework, not nursing-specific clinical guidance; third-party material may carry separate rights.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
creator: National Institute of Standards and Technology
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
claims_supported: Generative AI introduces risks including confident false content, harmful bias, privacy exposure, and information-integrity problems.
Risk responses should be aligned to context, goals, and priorities.
limitations: General risk-management profile, not a clinical-use authorization; third-party material may carry separate rights.

title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
creator: World Health Organization
claims_supported: Ethics and human rights should be central to health-AI design, deployment, and use.
Accountability should remain responsive to healthcare workers and affected communities.
limitations: Cited without adapting or redistributing source text; the IGO license includes noncommercial and share-alike conditions.

title: Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule
creator: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
claims_supported: HIPAA protects certain individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by covered entities and business associates.
A summary is not a complete substitute for the governing rule or legal advice.
limitations: United States-focused summary; applicability varies, state and other laws may add duties, and this Pack does not provide legal advice.

title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
creator: World Health Organization
claims_supported: Large multi-modal models can produce false, inaccurate, biased, or incomplete statements.
Health-related use requires defined tasks, stakeholder involvement, post-release auditing, and governance responsibilities.
limitations: Original synthesis and citation only; no WHO text, tables, figures, graphics, or marks are bundled. The official release is dated 18 January 2024, while catalog metadata may display a later date.

title: The Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in Nursing Practice
creator: American Nurses Association
claims_supported: Nursing values, caring relationships, and human agency remain central when AI is used in nursing contexts.
Nurses should participate in evaluating potential benefits and harms of AI-enabled systems.
limitations: Public access is not redistribution permission. Original synthesis and citation only; no ANA text, examples, layout, graphics, logos, or marks are bundled. This position does not authorize a clinical system or a particular use.

title: Digital health transformation and nursing practice
creator: International Council of Nurses
claims_supported: Nurses need digital-health competence and meaningful participation in design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.
Digital-health transformation should remain people-centred and attentive to equity, safety, security, reliability, and sustainability.
limitations: Public access is not redistribution permission. Original synthesis and citation only; no ICN text, lists, graphics, logos, or marks are bundled. This position does not authorize a clinical system or a particular use.
